# MapEat — Copilot instructions

MapEat (working name) is a private, shared restaurant journal for one couple: a map of real restaurants, dated visits with each person's own 1–10 review, photos (visit photos and place menu photos), a shared wishlist, and a timeline.

**Start every session by reading, in order:** `docs/status/handoff.md` (current status, working mode, next step — newest entries at top), `docs/product/implementation-plan.md` (roadmap M0–M6 with progress), and the "Decisions confirmed" section of `docs/product/design-spec.md`. As of November 3, 2026: M0 (foundation), M1 (map + OSM catalog), M2 (visits and both reviews) and M3 (wishlist, tags, timeline, map filters) are built, local on one phone; M4 (photos) is next; iPhone verification of M0–M3 is pending. Keep these files updated whenever status changes.

## Workspace layout and sources of truth

- Git repo: https://github.com/AgamDan/mapeat (branch `main`). The Expo app lives at the **repo root** (`src/`, `assets/`, `app.json`, `package.json`); all commands run from the root. It was moved out of `mapeat-starter/` on 2026-11-02 — older log entries still mention that folder.
- `docs/` — all project documentation, grouped by type and indexed in `docs/README.md`:
  - `docs/product/design-spec.md` — the first-release design. Distinguishes **confirmed** user decisions from **proposals** and lists open decisions. Read it before implementing any feature.
  - `docs/research/` — research backing decisions (e.g. Tel Aviv OSM + Wikimedia Commons coverage). Name new files `YYYY-MM-DD-topic.md`.
  - `docs/status/handoff.md` — running status log (newest entries at top) with environment history and blockers. Keep it updated when status changes.
- `AGENTS.md` — Expo-specific agent rules (summarized below).
- `.vscode/mcp.json` — workspace MCP servers: Playwright, and Supabase hosted MCP pinned to `read_only=true` (no Supabase project exists yet; keep it read-only).
- `.superpowers/` (browser wireframe mockups) and `.mapeat-recovery/` (old SDK 57 dependency backup) are gitignored scratch areas, not app code.

## Commands (run at the repo root)

```powershell
npm ci                       # first, on a fresh clone: node_modules is not committed (package-lock.json is)
npx expo start --go          # dev server for Expo Go on a physical iPhone (scan QR with Camera; same Wi-Fi)
npx expo start --go --clear  # same, clearing Metro cache
npx tsc --noEmit             # typecheck (must pass with 0 errors)
npx expo lint                # lint (ESLint 9 flat config: eslint.config.js + eslint-config-expo)
npx expo export --platform ios --output-dir $env:TEMP\mapeat-export  # bundle check without a phone
npm run catalog:build        # rebuild assets/catalog/israel.json from Geofabrik's free Israel OSM extract (~120 MB download to .cache/)
npx expo-doctor              # diagnose dependency/config issues
npx expo install <package>   # ALWAYS use this to add packages (SDK-compatible versions), not npm/yarn add
npx expo install --fix       # realign package versions to the SDK
```

- Without `node_modules`, `npx tsc` silently downloads the unrelated deprecated `tsc` npm package ("This is not the tsc command you are looking for") instead of TypeScript — install dependencies first.
- `expo-env.d.ts` and `.expo/types/router.d.ts` (both gitignored) are generated by `npx expo start` (not by `expo export`). After adding a route, typed `href`s fail `tsc` until the types regenerate: run `$env:CI='1'; npx expo start --go` briefly, then stop it. Avoid `folder/[param]/index.tsx` routes: `expo start` and `expo lint` generate different typed names for them; use flat files (`visit/[id].tsx`, `visit/review.tsx`).
- All database writes go through `src/data/write-queue.ts` (`writeTransaction` / `enqueueWrite`); never call `withExclusiveTransactionAsync` directly (unsupported on web, and parallel writers hit "database is locked"). Never nest queued calls.
- `metro.config.js` only adds what `expo-sqlite` needs for the web preview (`wasm` asset + COOP/COEP headers); `react-native-maps` has no web support, so the map has a `.web.tsx` stub.
- There is no test runner configured yet (no Jest); there are no tests to run individually.
- Development is on **Windows**: `npm run ios` / iOS Simulator does not work. Device testing is Expo Go on iPhone only.
- Never use `npm install --force` or `--legacy-peer-deps` to get past resolution errors; diagnose them.
- Do not run `npm audit fix --force`.
- Run lint and typecheck before declaring a task done; both currently pass cleanly, so any error is a regression.

## Expo SDK 58 — do not trust training data

- Stack: Expo `~58` (SDK 58 explicitly chosen — never downgrade to 57), React Native 0.88.1, React 19.3, TypeScript ~6.0 (strict), Expo Router with `typedRoutes` and `reactCompiler` experiments enabled in `app.json`.
- Before touching any Expo/RN API, fetch the versioned docs at `https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v58.0.0/` (or the index at `https://docs.expo.dev/llms.txt`). APIs change every SDK.
- The app runs in **Expo Go**, which only includes Expo's bundled native modules. Do not add libraries needing custom native code without explicit approval (that requires a development build). Native Google Maps is not available in iOS Expo Go.
- Never create/edit `ios/` or `android/` by hand (Continuous Native Generation); configure native behavior through `app.json` and config plugins.

## Code conventions

- Architecture and milestone order: `docs/product/implementation-plan.md`. Routes only in `src/app/` (`_layout.tsx` = providers + root `Stack`; `(tabs)/` = native tabs Map/Timeline; `welcome.tsx` first-launch language choice; `settings.tsx` modal). Shared UI in `src/components/`, feature logic in `src/features/<area>/`, persistence only through `src/data/` (local-first now, Supabase later — screens must not talk to storage directly).
- First launch is gated with `Stack.Protected` on `settings.language` (`null` until chosen) — don't add redirects for it.
- Import alias `@/*` → `src/*`, and `@/assets/*` → `assets/*`.
- Platform-specific files use the `.web.tsx` / `.web.ts` suffix next to the native file (e.g. `app-tabs.tsx` uses `expo-router/native-tabs`; `app-tabs.web.tsx` is the web variant). Keep both variants in sync when changing behavior.
- **i18n**: every UI string is a key in `src/i18n/en.ts` with a matching entry in `src/i18n/he.ts` (typed as `Translations`, so a missing key fails `tsc`). Use `useT()`; `useLanguage()` gives `language`/`direction`. User-written text is never translated.
- **RTL in Expo Go**: native `I18nManager.forceRTL` does not work in Expo Go. Direction is applied by the Yoga `direction` style on the root view + Stack `contentStyle`, and Expo Router's `LocaleProvider`. Use `start`/`end` (not `left`/`right`) for margins, padding, and positions. `ThemedText` sets `writingDirection` and leaves `textAlign` natural — don't hardcode `textAlign: 'left'`.
- **Theming** ("Mediterranean postcard"): colors only from `Colors.light/dark` in `src/constants/theme.ts` via `useTheme()` (respects the System/Light/Dark setting — never call RN `useColorScheme` directly); use `ThemedText`/`ThemedView` with `ThemeColor` keys. Fonts are Frank Ruhl Libre (Hebrew + Latin), referenced as `Fonts.regular|medium|bold|black` font families (one family per weight — don't use `fontWeight` with them). `Spacing` and `Radius` scales; `Postcard` is the signature card. Each person has an ink color (`personA`/`personB`).
- **Settings** (language, appearance) persist in AsyncStorage under `mapeat.settings.v1` via `SettingsProvider`/`useSettings()`.
- Kebab-case file names (`themed-text.tsx`, `use-theme.ts`); named exports for components/hooks, default export for route screens and `AppTabs`.

## Product rules that constrain implementation

These are confirmed user decisions; see the design spec (especially "Decisions confirmed November 2, 2026") for details and open questions.

- **Hard no-cost constraint**: no billing accounts, payment details, paid plans, metered APIs, or Apple Developer enrollment. If a step could cost money, explain the cost and STOP. Google Places/Google billing is excluded — do not ask to enable it again, and never scrape Google Maps.
- **Ask when uncertain**: proposals in the spec are not approved. Resolve open decisions (listed in the spec) with the user before implementing dependent features; don't guess on scope, permissions, spending, language, journal ownership, or rating semantics.
- **Bilingual**: Hebrew (RTL) and English (LTR) with in-app language switching. Translate UI labels and validation/error messages; user-written notes stay as written. Switching language must not lose an unsaved draft.
- **Data model**: Place and Visit are separate. One shared `Visit` (place + visit date) has one `VisitReview` per member (own 1–10 rating + notes). A partner's review attaches to the existing visit; a return visit creates a new visit. Never overwrite a visit/review or represent a missing review as rating 0. Store visit calendar date separately from created/updated timestamps (date-only must not shift across timezones).
- **Restaurant catalog**: restaurants must exist on the map with profiles before any visit (manual-only place entry is rejected). Source is OpenStreetMap: a built-in Israel file (`assets/catalog/israel.json`, built by `npm run catalog:build`, loaded into SQLite on first launch by `src/data/starter-catalog.ts`) plus live Overpass for areas outside it or older than 30 days, cached in SQLite by ~2 km tiles. Public Overpass is often overloaded (502/timeouts): requests are sequential with fallback servers, and failures stay quiet unless the map shows no places. Venue kinds: `restaurant`, `cafe`, `fast_food`, `bar`, `pub`, `ice_cream` (keep `VENUE_KINDS` and the build script's `KINDS` in sync). Keep "© OpenStreetMap contributors" reachable (ⓘ on the map, credit on the place profile). Only ~1% of venues link a photo: show Commons images only with author/license, otherwise a localized "No photo yet" placeholder. Profile photos never mix with the couple's private photos.
- **Map**: Apple Maps via `react-native-maps` (in Expo Go, $0, no key), wrapped in one app-owned map component. `expo-maps`/MapLibre need a custom build ($99/yr Apple Developer) — excluded. Apple's own POI labels can't be tapped for data. Custom `Marker` children need a non-flattened root (`collapsable={false}`) or the native marker shrinks and stops receiving taps; map taps also fall back to `venueAtPoint` (nearest drawn venue within 24 pt).
- **Private photos**: visit photos (addable anytime after a visit, by either member) and menu photos that belong to the place (addable before any visit). A couple's photo may be chosen explicitly as a private journal cover, never as a public profile photo.
- **Wishlist**: one shared wishlist; a place leaves it automatically only after its first visit is *successfully* saved. Either member may remove manually; visited places can carry a separate "want to go back" mark.
- **Reviews**: whole-number rating 1–10 is required, notes optional; place summary shows each person's own average side by side (never combined). Either member may edit or delete anything (with confirmation).
- **Reliability**: keep drafts until save succeeds; retries must not duplicate records (stable submission IDs); photo upload failures don't undo a saved visit.
- **Local-first, then backend**: until milestone M5, data lives on the phone (one phone, "Writing as" switch between the two people). Later: Supabase Free (Auth, Postgres, private Storage) with Row Level Security for member-only access; Sign in with Apple via `expo-apple-authentication`; partner joins via invite link + 6-digit code. No secrets in client code or source control. Hiding UI is not access control.
- Audience is just the couple on two iPhones via Expo Go with the dev server running; public release, Android, and standalone distribution are out of scope.
